subject: Deployment safety net: canary criteria, automatic fallback and pin request
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@nh-health.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Deployment safety net: canary criteria, automatic fallback and pin request

Samira —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. As discussed, Nimbus Health will be running the new med-summarization endpoint against a subset of production traffic. To reduce risk to your SLOs while we evaluate model v3, we want to request a short-term deployment safety net to be codified in the SLA carve-out: an automated canary with deterministic fallback and a temporary version-pinning option for the first 72 hours of progressive rollout.

High-level ask: grant Redwood the ability to execute an automated fallback to the previous pinned model (v2.7) or shift traffic to the dedicated lower-latency instance pool if the canary breaches the agreed triggers below. We'll sign the SLA carve-out (attached) and set a short security/ops review window.

Attached: canary-config-v3.yaml (proposed thresholds) and the blank SLA carve-out form.

Proposed safety net (we are flexible on thresholds — listing conservative starting values):
- Traffic ramp: 2% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% over 8 hours with 30–60 minute hold at each step
- Canary duration per step: minimum 30 minutes after steady-state
- Automatic fallback triggers (any of):
  - p95 latency increase > 40% relative to baseline for 10 minutes
  - absolute p95 latency > 350 ms for > 5 minutes
  - error rate > 1.5% for 5 minutes
  - tail timeout spikes (>= 10 timeouts in 5 min window)
- Pin behavior: on fallback we will pin traffic to previous model version for at least 2 hours and freeze roll-forward until a postmortem is agreed
- Monitoring/alerts: real-time p95/p99, 5xx rate, request timeout count, model output-quality regression alarm (if eval harness detects >3 regressions on golden set)

Operational notes:
- We will perform progressive KV cache warm-up (warm-up calls prior to ramp) and a synthetic traffic health-probe.
- Fallback path: switch to v2.7 variant + route 20% of traffic to the dedicated low-latency pool for 30 minutes to validate stability before full re-pinning.

Can you confirm this approach and if Procurement/Legal need different language in the carve-out? If you sign off, we'll open the SLA exception request and schedule the rollout window for next Tuesday (11/17).

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
E: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai | M: (415) 555-0192

-----
Attachment: canary-config-v3.yaml (stated thresholds)
Attachment: sla-carveout-form.pdf

From: Samira Patel <samira@nh-health.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Health - infra-team <infra-team@nh-health.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment safety net: canary criteria, automatic fallback and pin request

Evelyn —

Appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifying questions from infra and compliance before we approve: 
1) Who owns the automatic fallback action and audit trail? We need an immutable log and the ability to manually override within 10 minutes.
2) Can you confirm the exact change window and if the fallback is fully automated (no manual gate) or semi-automatic with a 5-min hold?
3) For pinning: how long can you keep our production traffic pinned to v2.7? We want a maximum pin of 48 hours unless we jointly agree to extend.
4) Is there a way to route traffic by region during canary? We only want US traffic in the first wave.

Also, the absolute p95 threshold of 350 ms is close to our internal p95 SLO (320 ms). Would Redwood be comfortable shifting to a relative delta trigger only? Our worry is too many false positives during normal traffic spikes.

If you can respond here, I'll loop in Procurement for the carve-out review.

— Samira
Samira Patel
Director, Infrastructure — Nimbus Health
samira@nh-health.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Samira Patel <samira@nh-health.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment safety net: canary criteria, automatic fallback and pin request

Samira / team —

Short answers first: fallback is automated (policy engine triggers), every decision is logged to the deployment audit-stream (immutable append-only); manual override is available from Console with a 10-minute confirmation step. We can make the fallback semi-automatic (5-minute auto-execute unless manually cancelled) if that is preferable.

On thresholds: happy to switch to relative-only triggers for latency to reduce false positives. Suggested tuning:
- Relative p95 increase > 35% versus rolling 24h baseline for 10m -> trigger
- Absolute p95 guard: > 500 ms for >5m (emergency guardrail only)
- Error rate > 1% for 5m -> trigger

Operational plan (detailed):
- Traffic ramp plan: 2% (15m) -> 10% (30m) -> 25% (60m) -> 50% (2h). Each step has a minimum steady-state hold and health-check gating.
- Health-checks: probe endpoint /_health returns 200 in <200ms for 5 consecutive probes spaced 15s apart before progressing.
- Cache warm-up: pre-warm with synthetic keys (script included in attachment) for 10 minutes before moving past 2%
- Fallback action:
  1) Policy engine flips traffic to pinned model v2.7 via traffic-router (atomic change).
  2) System creates an audit event: fallback:{timestamp, metric_snapshot, reason, actor:auto-policy}
  3) Pin remains in effect for 2 hours by default; can be shortened/extended via Console with audit entry.
- Roll-forward lock: until a post-incident review is completed, rollout remains blocked for that deployment id.

Sample snippet (canary-config-v3.yaml):
---
canary:
  ramps: [2, 10, 25, 50]
  step_hold: [15m, 30m, 60m, 2h]
  gate: health_check
triggers:
  latency_relative_pct: 35
  latency_absolute_ms: 500
  error_rate_pct: 1.0
fallback_policy:
  action: pin_to_previous
  pin_duration: 2h
  audit: true
---

We will restrict initial wave to US only (region routing is supported).

Next steps: Evelyn / Rachel to confirm final wording for the carve-out and whether Nimbus wants the fallback to be semi-automatic (5-min confirmation) or fully automatic. If you pick semi-automatic, we'll implement the 5-min cancellation window in the policy engine.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

-----
Attachment referenced: canary-config-v3.yaml (snippet)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
To: Samira Patel <samira@nh-health.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Deployment safety net: canary criteria, automatic fallback and pin request

Samira —

Thanks for the careful review. We're aligned on keeping the initial triggers conservative and moving to relative-only latency triggers to reduce noise. For Procurement: please have Nimbus sign the attached SLA carve-out with these bullets captured exactly as Marcus summarized. A few clarifications I added for Legal:
- Pin duration: set to 48 hours maximum in the carve-out (we'll default to 2 hours operationally unless you elect to extend)
- Manual override: console-level control with 10-min confirmation window; every override creates an immutable audit event
- Region restriction: first wave limited to US traffic only; EU/APAC excluded unless explicitly agreed

Operational commitments we will add to the carve-out appendix: runbook link, postmortem timeline (72h), and dedicated on-call for the rollout window (Redwood on-call + Nimbus infra buddy).

Evelyn, Marcus, Aditya: please open the formal SLA exception request and /cc Procurement contact once Samira confirms. Samira — if you confirm semi-automatic (5-min cancellation) or fully automatic, we'll tune the policy engine accordingly.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
rachel_kim@redwood.ai
